alt.en: The lower part of a worn telegraph form with purple ruled lines, filled in by hand: "To Spafford", "Received at Chicago Ills Dec 2d 5 40 am 1873", "159 LaSalle St Chicago", then "Saved alone what shall I do. Mrs Goodwin Children Willie Culver lost go with Lorriaux until answer reply", an address at 64 Rue Aboukir, Paris, and the signature "Spafford". The form's printed heading is not shown.
alt.es: La parte de abajo de un formulario de telégrafo gastado, con renglones morados, escrito a mano: "To Spafford", "Received at Chicago Ills Dec 2d 5 40 am 1873", "159 LaSalle St Chicago", y después "Saved alone what shall I do. Mrs Goodwin Children Willie Culver lost go with Lorriaux until answer reply", una dirección en el 64 de la Rue Aboukir, en París, y la firma "Spafford". No se ve el encabezado impreso del formulario.

caption.en: Anna Spafford's cable from Wales after the wreck, as it was written out on arrival in Chicago on 2 December 1873: "Saved alone what shall I do."
caption.es: El cable que Anna Spafford envió desde Gales después del naufragio, tal como se copió al llegar a Chicago el 2 de diciembre de 1873: "Saved alone what shall I do" (salvada, sola; qué debo hacer).

source: Telegram from Anna Spafford to Horatio Gates Spafford re being "Saved alone" among her traveling party in the shipwreck of the Ville du Havre, received at Chicago, 2 December 1873 (Atlantic Cable Message form)
callNumber: American Colony in Jerusalem Collection, Part I, Box 1, Folder 6; digital id mamcol.011
licenceEvidence: Written December 1873; its author Anna T. Spafford died in 1923 (LoC record: "Spafford, Anna T., 1842-1923"); printed form 1873. LoC rights statement for the collection: "The Library of Congress has reviewed the copyright status of the documents presented from collection and is not aware of any U.S. copyright or any other restrictions in the documents." Faithful scan of a flat document (see rights.md).
credit: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, American Colony in Jerusalem Collection

alt.en: A handwritten page in purple ink on ruled paper, creased into quarters, with the hymn's four verses, from "When peace like a river, attendeth my way" to a last line ending "oh my soul!". Faint pencil words sit in the left margin and below the last line. The printed hotel letterhead at the top of the sheet is not shown.
alt.es: Una página escrita a mano con tinta morada en papel rayado, doblada en cuatro, con las cuatro estrofas del himno, desde "When peace like a river, attendeth my way" hasta un último verso que termina "oh my soul!". Hay palabras tenues a lápiz en el margen izquierdo y bajo el último verso. No se ve el membrete impreso del hotel en lo alto de la hoja.

caption.en: Spafford's own handwritten copy of his four verses, on the notepaper of a Chicago hotel, the Brevoort House; it bears no date, so when he wrote it out is not known for certain.
caption.es: La copia manuscrita de Spafford de sus cuatro estrofas, en papel de carta de un hotel de Chicago, el Brevoort House; no lleva fecha, así que no se sabe con certeza cuándo la escribió.

source: Draft manuscript copy of hymn "It is Well With My Soul" by Horatio Gates Spafford, ink on Brevoort House (Chicago) letterhead, undated, page 1
callNumber: American Colony in Jerusalem Collection, Part I, Box 1, Folder 11; digital id mamcol.016
licenceEvidence: Written about 1873 to 1878 (LoC); author Horatio Gates Spafford, 1828-1888; the hymn itself was published in 1876 and 1878. LoC rights statement for the collection: "The Library of Congress has reviewed the copyright status of the documents presented from collection and is not aware of any U.S. copyright or any other restrictions in the documents." Faithful scan of a flat document (see rights.md).
credit: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, American Colony in Jerusalem Collection

alt.en: A page of printed music numbered 78, headed "No. 76. It is Well with My Soul." in black-letter type, with "He hath delivered my soul in peace." Ps. 55: 18, and the credits "H. G. Spafford" and "P. P. Bliss, by per." Four systems of treble and bass staves carry verses 1 and 2 and the chorus, "It is well, it is well with my soul"; verses 3 and 4 are printed as text below the music.
alt.es: Una página de música impresa, numerada 78, con el encabezado "No. 76. It is Well with My Soul." en letra gótica, el versículo "He hath delivered my soul in peace." Ps. 55: 18 y los créditos "H. G. Spafford" y "P. P. Bliss, by per." Cuatro sistemas de pentagramas en clave de sol y de fa llevan las estrofas 1 y 2 y el estribillo, "It is well, it is well with my soul"; las estrofas 3 y 4 van impresas como texto bajo la música.

caption.en: The earliest known printing of Spafford's words with Bliss's tune, No. 76 in Gospel Hymns No. 2 (1876), headed with Psalm 55:18 and signed "P. P. Bliss, by per.", by permission.
caption.es: La impresión más antigua que se conoce de la letra de Spafford con la melodía de Bliss, el n.º 76 de Gospel Hymns No. 2 (1876), encabezado con el Salmo 55:18 y firmado "P. P. Bliss, by per.", es decir, con permiso.

source: P. P. Bliss and Ira D. Sankey, Gospel Hymns No. 2 (New York: Biglow & Main; Cincinnati: John Church & Co., 1876), No. 76, p. 78, "It is Well with My Soul"
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Princeton Theological Seminary Library SCC; OCLC 1046535742; Internet Archive hymnsno02blis
licenceEvidence: Printed 1876; Bliss died 1876, Spafford 1888, Sankey 1908. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A yellowed book page inside a red ruled border, numbered 44, headed "It Is Well With My Soul." in black-letter type, with "JOHN XV. 16." below. The first three verses follow, the first opening with a large letter W in a scrollwork frame. There is no music.
alt.es: Una página amarillenta de un libro, dentro de un marco de líneas rojas, numerada 44, con el encabezado "It Is Well With My Soul." en letra gótica y debajo "JOHN XV. 16." Siguen las tres primeras estrofas; la primera empieza con una W grande dentro de un marco de volutas. No hay música.

caption.en: Spafford printed the poem again, without music, in his own collection, Waiting for the Morning (Chicago, 1878), page 44.
caption.es: Spafford volvió a imprimir el poema, sin música, en su propia colección, Waiting for the Morning (Chicago, 1878), página 44.

source: Waiting for the Morning, and Other Poems, by the author of "Twenty Reasons for Believing the Coming of the Lord is Nigh" [Horatio G. Spafford] (Chicago: F. H. Revell, 1878), p. 44, "It Is Well With My Soul"
library: Library of Congress (digitized by the Internet Archive)
